slides.title: prompts to create and sell a digital product this weekend
slides.sub: Idea Saturday morning, first sale by Sunday night.
slides.voiceover: Here are seven prompts to build and sell a digital product in one weekend.

slides.name: The Product Finder
slides.prompt: Act as a digital product strategist. I'm good at [SKILL] and know [AUDIENCE]. Give me 7 digital product ideas I can finish in one weekend (templates, checklists, guides, prompt packs), the problem each solves, a fair price, and which one has the **FASTEST FIRST SALE**.

lines: Fastest sale: low price, instant use

slides.voiceover: One. Get seven weekend-sized product ideas, ranked by how fast they can sell.

slides.name: The Outline Maker
slides.sub: The full product plan in 5 minutes.
slides.prompt: Create the complete outline for [PRODUCT IDEA] for [AUDIENCE]: sections, what goes into each, examples to include, and the one 'quick win' the buyer gets in the **FIRST 10 MINUTES**. Keep it small enough to finish in 2 days.
slides.tip: If the outline has more than 6 sections, cut it — a smaller finished product beats a bigger unfinished one.
slides.voiceover: Two. Turn one idea into a full outline, small enough to finish in two days.

slides.name: The Content Drafter
slides.sub: Write the product section by section.
slides.prompt: Write section [NUMBER] of my product [PRODUCT NAME] based on this outline: [PASTE OUTLINE]. Practical, specific, with one example and one mini exercise. Plain language for [AUDIENCE], no padding, and flag anything I should **CHECK** myself.

lines: Flagged to check: the local tax line

slides.voiceover: Three. Draft the product section by section, with a mini exercise in each.

slides.name: The Sales Page
slides.sub: A page that explains and sells.
slides.prompt: Write a short sales page for [PRODUCT NAME] at [$PRICE]: a headline, the problem, what's inside as bullet points, who it's for and **NOT FOR**, 3 honest FAQs, and a clear buy button text. No fake testimonials, no fake scarcity.
slides.tip: Keep the 'who it's not for' line — it reads as honest, and it filters out refund requests later.
slides.voiceover: Four. Get a sales page that's honest, specific, and ready to publish.

slides.name: The Launch Posts
slides.prompt: Write 5 social media posts to launch [PRODUCT NAME] on [PLATFORM]: a behind-the-scenes post, a problem post, a sneak peek, a 'who it's for' post, and a launch-day post. Give each a hook and a caption with **ONE** call to action.

lines: Post 1 hook: 'I built this in a weekend'
Post 4 hook: 'this is for you if...'

slides.voiceover: Five. Get five launch posts, each with one clear call to action.

slides.name: The Price Tester
slides.prompt: Help me price [PRODUCT NAME] for [AUDIENCE]. Compare 3 price points ([$LOW], [$MID], [$HIGH]), what each signals, a bundle or upsell idea, and a simple way to test prices in the **FIRST 2 WEEKS**.
slides.tip: Launch at the middle price — it's easier to add a discount later than to raise a price your first buyers saw.
slides.voiceover: Six. Compare three price points instead of guessing one.

slides.name: The Feedback Loop
slides.prompt: Write a short thank-you email for buyers of [PRODUCT NAME] with 3 questions that tell me what to improve, and plan version 2: what to add based on likely answers, and how to turn happy buyers into **REVIEWS** without pressure.

lines: Q: what almost stopped you buying?
V2 idea: add a quick-start checklist
Ask for a review only after a 'thanks!'

slides.voiceover: Seven. Turn your first buyers into the feedback that builds version two.

slides.title: Get more out of this pack
items: Idea, then outline, then draft — each prompt feeds the next in one chat, so nothing gets rebuilt twice.
A template or checklist ships in a weekend; a full course doesn't. Small and finished beats big and stuck.
Launch with the outline and one strong section done — the sales page and the first buyers tell you what to polish.
slides.voiceover: Run these in order, pick the smallest idea, and sell before it's perfect.
